brief_summary: Side-by-side cross-section comparing a rigid tray-mount case, where the plate is bolted flush to the case wall and switch resonance transmits straight into the shell, against the Bakeneko65's o-ring gasket-mount case, where the plate floats inside a gasket boundary that breaks the resonance path before it reaches the aluminum shell.
data_sources: apps/web/src/content/articles/bento-box-theme-build.mdx § 'Gasket isolation is why a bright switch housing doesn't sound cheap here' — 'PC housings have a known acoustic tendency: they read brighter and more resonant than nylon or POM housings on a rigid mounting platform'

apps/web/src/content/articles/bento-box-theme-build.mdx § 'Gasket isolation is why a bright switch housing doesn't sound cheap here' — 'An o-ring gasket mount decouples the plate-and-PCB assembly from the case wall instead of screwing it down directly, which means high-frequency resonance generated at the switch has to cross a compliant boundary before it reaches the aluminum shell'
data/boards/bakeneko65.json — 'Cast-aluminum 65% with an o-ring gasket mount, FR4 plate, and a hotswap QMK/VIA PCB'
